item.title: SCP-XXXX: Empathic Erhu (seeking greenlights): SCP-XXXX: Empathic Erhu (seeking greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
A musical instrument that creates instantaneous empathy, and the ethical/philosophical conflicts within the Foundation that result from it.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mythological, Philosophical

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP layout with some tests and a few cross-tests

Elevator Pitch:

  • SCP-XXXX is an emotokinetic1 erhu that when played causes anyone who hears it to receive all of the emotions and underlying memories of the player.
  • SCP-XXXX achieves this "instantaneous empathy" by generating empathons, the elementary subatomic particle of the psychospace responsible for human emotion.2
  • SCP-XXXX can transmit any human emotion, resulting in a conflict between the O5 Council and the Ethics Committee concerning how best to use SCP-XXXX.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is hand-delivered to the Foundation by the headless god of perseverance Xíng Tiān, who says that it will help humanity by bringing individuals together. Testing reveals that SCP-XXXX does this by using empathons to broadcast the emotions of the person playing SCP-XXXX.

+ show block
– hide block

However, because SCP-XXXX can use empathons to transmit any human emotion, a conflict arises between the O-5 Council, who want to weaponize SCP-XXXX, and the Ethics Committee, who want to use SCP-XXXX as a mode of communication with sapient SCP's.

This conflict is resolved when Xíng Tiān hijacks SCP-XXXX and gives all the D-class at Site-64 the ability to emotokinetically communicate with each other, allowing them to cooperate and pool their knowledge of certain SCP's to coordinate a prison break that leads to the loss of several SCP personnel.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: SCP-XXXX is an anomalous musical instrument that generates instantaneous empathy, and this emotokinetic ability results in an ethical conflict within the Foundation. SCP-XXXX also expands upon the lore of the psychospace and certain humanoid SCP's such as SCP-5027 and SCP-5278.

Additional Notes:

  • I know that Series I SCP's like SCP-187 and SCP-682 are fairly overdone; I would be happy to substitute them for more recent SCP's. Essentially, I need an SCP with precognitive abilities and an SCP that's physically invincible.
  • I read SCP-5027 a few weeks ago and loved the premise, although I did get bummed out by the ending. If the author of SCP-5027 is okay with it, I would like to use SCP-XXXX to give SCP-5027 a somewhat happier ending (nothing like leaving containment, but at least an ending where SCP-5027 can be treated like a human being).
  • Lastly, thank you for reading this SCP idea! Any guidance is much appreciated, and I look forward to hearing from you!

Collapsible edited as the post was still rather long. ~Zyn

Footnotes
1. capable of controlling the emotions of sentient beings
2. similar to the Higgs Boson being responsible for mass or the photon being responsible for light

item.title: [Seeking Greenlight] Unsolved Hypercube: Re: [Seeking Greenlight] Unsolved Hypercube
item.content:encoded:
Hello SuperAmazingTaco! let's take a look :) welcome to the site!

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a Rubik's cube which, when close to being solved, begins to behave like a 4-dimensional Rubik's cube to prevent itself from being solved. When it nears being solved again it will instead begin to behave like a 5-dimensional Rubik's cube, and so on. After being far away enough from being solved it will revert to a lower dimension. These processes have a consistent order and pattern. As a byproduct SCP-XXXXs mass increases with each dimension over 3 dimensions it contains (starting with the mass of a regular Rubik's cube) as well as giving off a small amount of ionizing radiation. This increase in mass and the presence of radiation grows exponentially with each additional dimension.

My main issue with the concept, is the skips overall purpose. what is the skip meant to do? whats the reason for it existing?

My second biggest issue comes from the effects it has; Currently, they don't really feel related to the skip. There also isn't much context as to why radiation and mass adds onto the skip after each near solve.- Currently these two aspects aren't really explained or expanded upon in the narrative, which causes the skip to feel a bit disjointed.

The narrative:

Central Narrative: The central narrative of this piece would take the form of several testing logs where Dr. Cass experiments with SCP-XXXX and its unusual properties. Over time they work towards the possibility of using SCP-XXXXs radioactive properties for fuel in a power generator based on fusion reactor designs. This pursuit eventually leads to conflict with the site director who is against the idea. By the end of it the site director removes Dr. Cliff as the project lead (instead having them as a project advisor) and further experimentation with SCP-XXXX is delayed until a new project lead can be established.

How would you plan to execute this idea in a draft? currently the narrative doesn't show much of a progression.- how do tensions rise between the researcher and site director? how do ideas suddenly shift to nuclear reactor? what ends up causing the researcher to be removed from their position?

While I'm liking the conflict here, the site director doesn't seem to have a reason to be so opposed to this. Considering there's no immediate dangers (at least from whats described). It's odd that he/she would be ready to remove the researcher from their position in order to prevent further discussion on the topic. As a result, the conflict feels a bit forced/in-genuine as the opposition just sounds like their trying to make problems.

- Furthermore, it makes it harder for me to get invested in the characters (and/or get emotionally invested in the narrative). As the characters don't have any clear or conflicting goals.

Along with this, the narrative doesn't give much of a setup; as it stands, there isn't much on how the Foundation initially found the skip, or what caught their attention (the Rubik's cube on its own is rather a subtle anomaly, so it very likely the foundation didn't immediately suspect it).

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight.

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques/perspectives in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

RED

item.title: A Thousand Door (Seeking Greenlight): Re: A Thousand Door (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Hi! Thank you for the critique, it helps me a lot! I have to answer your questions and more explanation regarding my idea.

+ My response and more explanation
- Here it goes

What is SCP trying to prove?

It tries to tell that The Glorification that is shown in the place (which is a historical museum) shouldn't be something to be proud of, the effect that was brought by the colony may be good, but it was built based on the misery of the people from the past. The Room represents how the people of the past felt back then, the tragedy that they have to go through and this room is trying to retell the story of what happened. To remind everyone, especially the events like that in the past shouldn't be forgotten, which most the people already did, as if nothing happened. The emotions, feelings, anger, etc are represented in this room that projects that current era.

Here's an alternate idea that you can choose to reject/accept

I may have not explained it all in my previous response, but I think my idea had some similarities with yours, and I'll try to explain it as best as I can.

I do agree about the Pocket Dimension that you mentioned above is similar to my so-called Room Projection of that time, my basic idea is that when the person (let's just say D-Class) enters the room of that place, it will also recreate the exact event, place, and time of the tragedy happening inside the room.

I already have created a scene where this place was used to be known as the biggest railroad station by the Dutch colony, it was full of railroad workers that are forced to work there and at some time there is a rebellion happening that some of the workers started a movement to take over this place. This event happened after the D-Class enter this room, and the D-Class had to partake of that event, while the people knew or acknowledge the existence of the D-Class such as giving guns to help the rebellion despite he's wearing a modern-day D-Class shirt, but they didn't know about it and sees it as a normal railroad worker. This is the part where the D-Class also had to "feel what they have gone through", the struggle that they have to face, and then finish it until that event is over. If he died in the event, that means that the D-Class is also dead in real life, as in failed to accomplish their goal, but if he succeeds, he falls asleep to take a rest because he already accomplished the goal in the event and woke up again in a different room that they have to proceed to go down with stairs and open the door to the next event.

While it may have some similarities to your idea, but I didn't think about that emotional side especially about the family of that person. I really love your suggestion about putting the explorer's wife, son, and relatives in the event, to make this explorer emotionally vulnerable towards the situation that he/she has gotten into. I would like to ask for your permission to grab your idea, and maybe I changed it a bit by making it like some of the people in that event is replaced with the close relative of the explorer, whether it's their son, spouse, cousin, best friend, etc, to fight also in a scene where the person that the explorer really knew is about to die not because they chose to be in this situation, but because they were forced to, just like how the people from the past are being forced to do so.


If there's still any question, doubts or need more extensive explanation towards something I just mentioned above, feel free to critique it and I'll be gladly to improve this concept further. Thanks in Advance!

item.title: On the Shores of Paradise: Re: On the Shores of Paradise
item.content:encoded:
Hey again, thanks for the crit!
Sorry for the delayed response, an unfortunate cmd+r set me back after I had formulated most of my reply (along with other things). But anyway…

Here are my responses!
Woooooosh

First things first, the easier part of your crit to answer.

Besides that, I should mention that I’m rather confused as to how most of this would be documented in clinical tone. To the best of my knowledge, folks scrambling to survive an apocalypse or hypnotized by plants might not keep up to date on their documentation.

Well, most of this will be documented through emails, site memos, chat logs, security footage, etc, instead of official documentation. In case you're wondering how the sense of mystery would be preserved with security footage, it'll be mostly obscured by leaves and the like (the plants would grow on the ceiling for stealth).

And now the second part.

My main concern here is that the anomaly lessens your emotional plot beats. […] How do you plan to avoid that?

By building off of P1 (the protagonist against evacuating) being incarcerated in their cell, and thus avoiding P2's (the protagonist for evacuating) speech and exodus of the town into the gateway1, I plan to create an entirely new ethical dilemma that builds off of the first.
The story goes:
- P1, taking a USB full of the contents of their computer, escapes the town and is rescued by Foundation personnel
- They're understandably traumatised and tormented by survivor's guilt, and develop PTSD and depression2. This is revealed in a psychological evaluation
- However, the Foundation begins to suspect something is wrong after P1 suffers numerous seizures, bouts of uncharacteristic and extremely erratic behaviour, and eventually, a hemorrhagic stroke (note that they are the only person the Foundation has in custody who has had contact with the anomaly)
- Blood tests reveal the presence of anomalous prions within P1's brain. Through extensive testing, these prions are found to be thaumaturgically charged and, through a poorly understood mechanism, partially 'link' P1's mind to the large, central hive mind I mentioned in my summary
- Said hive mind uses the prions to both communicate with and physically damage (haemorrhage) P1, for the purpose of convincing them to return to the gateway, in exchange for P2 and the numerous other people it had taken (revealed in another interview)
- Through the interview, the Foundation finds out that 1) The prions appear through a chemical/thaumic reaction after ingesting the hallucinogen, 2) the anomaly feeds off of brain activity and converts it to energy (this process creates huge amounts of energy) using the prions as a transfer mechanism, 3) everyone considered lost to the anomaly is in fact alive (but in a vegetative state), and 4) P1 is their only method of communicating with/discreetly spying upon the anomaly
- Point 4 is true because testing with others has only resulted in the participants immediately succumbing to brain haemorrhage (the anomaly finds no point in keeping them alive as it cannot bargain with them)
- As such, their only option of neutralising the anomaly is to find out its weakness through P1 with subtle memetic influence, while keeping them (and thus the hive mind) completely oblivious to the Foundation's true goal. Unfortunately, this means constantly reinjecting them with prions to keep the connection stable, making their mental suffering much worse
- As the 05 Council deems the Ethics Committee emotionally compromised by the circumstances (P1 was their friend, and their judgement would be affected by that), they decide to come to a decision on their own, and, after much deliberation, the motion passes that P1 should be used as a method of spying (Operation: Verdant Sleeper)
- Article ends with the message that the operation is in effect, results pending

My main concern is that this may not in fact solve the original problem (lessens emotional impact) rather than add something else entirely. Hopefully not though.
Also, the anomaly wants P1 (and P1 only) because it finds their thoughts incredibly tasty (extreme grief and guilt stemming from the anomaly itself —> yummy). This is documented in P1's journal, which is covertly read when they are asleep. Breach of privacy I know, but this is for the sake of the world.


Anyway, that's it for my response ('twas a big one, I know, sorry about that). Thanks for reading, and hope this assuages your concerns!
Footnotes
1. P1, unfortunately, sees P2 (and many others) dragged into the gateway.
2. I don't want this to be perceived as a liberal application of mental disorders onto a character for sympathy/drama, I'm simply trying to emulate what I perceive to be the reaction of someone experienced in ethics being directly involved in the needless death of thousands of people+their friend

item.title: Need a concept greenlit: Forum Criticism Team - Junior Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
instantramen3160, per the required forum guidelines:

Do not link to a sandbox unless a reviewer asks to see a draft.

Instead, please use the standardized template for concepts found here: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-13282684/required-reading:how-to-use-this-forum-ideas

Additionally, please do not copy-paste portions of a sandbox draft into the template in lieu of actually filling out the sections. If you are unsure of what the post should look like, look around other threads within this forum.

Once you have reviewed the guidelines, please edit your post to the correct format rather than creating a new thread, and if you are having trouble editing, click the "edit" function under the "options" tab to the lower right of your post. Please feel free to then reach out to a reviewer for your concept: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-13282692/how-to-get-more-reviews
